run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: I could not tie request REQ-EU-8K4M2 to any service: the trace and metrics backends returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call during the whole Run, and no available log or document contains that identifier. What is observable: the Elasticsearch source holds only app-185-geo-* indices (1,620 indices), and the only documents inside the authorized window (162, all stamped 2026-11-21T04:50:00Z) are identical INFO 'Request completed successfully' entries with response_time_ms=150 for all 27 services in all six regions, including eu-west and eu-central, so that dataset shows no European latency anomaly. The otel-demo cluster shows no application failure evidence: all 22 pods are Running/Ready, application logs contain successful PlaceOrder/payment/email flows up to 04:51:26Z and only startup DNS/export noise at 04:23-04:24, there is no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota, the node is Ready without pressure, and all fault-injection flags in flagd-config (including paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, imageSlowLoad) are at defaultVariant 'off'. The only application-level alert rule defined is CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (>50% error ratio on checkout PlaceOrder server spans), but no Prometheus or Jaeger data was reachable to read its state or any span. The pods' restarts at 04:23:46 were a node-wide sandbox change affecting every pod including the monitoring stack, not a service-specific fault. No service can be named as affected or as root cause from the evidence obtained.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch source contains only app-185-geo-<region>-<service>-2024.01.xx style indices: the '*log*' listing returned 60 of them, and filtering all 1,620 indices for names not beginning 'app-185-geo' returned an empty list, so no other index family is present.

Inside the authorized window Elasticsearch holds 162 documents, all timestamped 2026-11-21T04:50:00Z; aggregation shows 27 documents for each of ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, eu-west, us-east and us-west, every document level INFO with message 'Request completed successfully', and response_time_ms average = maximum = 150 for every region, including eu-west and eu-central.

All 22 otel-demo pods received a 'Pod sandbox changed, it will be killed and re-created' (SandboxChanged) event at 2026-11-21T04:23:46Z, containers were Created/Started at 04:23:47-04:24:34Z, and the email container's previous instance logged 'Gracefully stopping, waiting for requests to finish' at 2026-11-21T04:07:51Z, i.e. the whole workload set restarted together rather than one service failing.

All 22 otel-demo pods are Running and their containers ready; each has restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated.reason 'Unknown' and exitCode 255, i.e. one restart from the 04:23 sandbox change and no crash-looping container.

The flagd-config ConfigMap holds demo.flagd.json with 11 fault-injection flags (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad), and every one of them is at defaultVariant 'off'.

The Prometheus configuration in otel-demo defines exactly one application alert, CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, firing when more than 50% of checkout PlaceOrder server spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, service_name=checkout, span_kind=SPAN_KIND_SERVER, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR) are errors over 5m for 2m at severity critical.

Checkout application logs in the window show repeated successful order flows ('[PlaceOrder] user_id=...', 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)', 'order confirmation email sent to ...') continuing through 2026-11-21T04:51:26Z.

Payment logs in the window contain structured 'Charge request received.' entries carrying trace_id values (e.g. trace_id e916e852b8d114f6c8046673ceb31c28 at 04:41:19Z through trace_id 154b21e72e257922e22a78ceb1f865b3 at 04:51:26Z); none of the read lines contains the identifier REQ-EU-8K4M2.

The only error lines in the ad and recommendation containers are startup DNS/export failures at 04:23:55-04:24:26Z ('Failed to resolve name ... flagd', 'UnknownHostException: otel-collector', 'Transient error StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE ... exporting logs to otel-collector:4317'), i.e. bring-up noise right after the 04:23 restart.
The cluster has no NetworkPolicy objects and no ResourceQuota objects, and its single node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy pod's nginx container has restartCount 3; its previous instance started 04:24:05Z and terminated with exitCode 1, reason Error at 04:24:10Z after logging '[emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"'; the current container has been running since 04:24:34Z and the pod has been Ready since 04:24:35Z.

Namespace app-101 runs Loki (image grafana/loki:2.9.0, configmap loki-config) and a promtail configmap whose scrape job 'payment-api' ships /var/log/*.log to http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/push with json parsing of timestamp/level/message/service/pod — these application logs are shipped to Loki, not to the Elasticsearch indices or to pod stdout that the enabled tools can read.

The frontend container has almost no application log output in the window: 38 lines from the previous instance (through 2026-11-20T16:33:42Z) and 12 lines from the current instance starting 2026-11-21T04:23:50Z, and the lines matching REQ/request_id are only the 'node --require ./Instrumentation.js server.js' startup command. The frontend-proxy emitted only Envoy startup/config lines from 04:23:48Z and a 'shutting down parent after drain' line at 04:39:58Z.

Rejected: that the app-185-geo datasets show the Europe slowdown. Within the window all six regions including eu-west and eu-central report the identical 150 ms, INFO, 'Request completed successfully' records, so those documents neither locate a slow region nor identify any failing service.

Rejected: that a pod restart or crash inside otel-demo is the fault. The 04:23:46Z SandboxChanged events hit every pod in the namespace simultaneously (including jaeger, prometheus and kube-state-metrics), pod restartCount is 1 with reason Unknown/exit 255, and no service-level error burst accompanies it, so this is a node/runtime-level restart, not a service failure.

Hypothesis (unsupported by observed failures): the customer's slow/erroring request most plausibly belongs to the checkout PlaceOrder path or its payment dependency, because the only application alert in this environment targets checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and the flagd configuration contains payment/checkout failure switches — but those flags are now all 'off', and no checkout or payment error, trace or metric was observed, so this remains unproven.

gaps: Every Jaeger call in this Run failed with status error / reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (traces_list_services at 04:52:00Z, 04:52:02Z, 04:52:16Z, 04:54:15Z, 04:55:46Z; traces_search at 04:52:19Z, 04:52:23Z, 04:53:11Z, 04:53:41Z, 04:54:59Z; traces_search_by_tags at 04:54:45Z; traces_list_operations at 04:53:01Z; traces_query_trace_by_id at 04:55:22Z), so request REQ-EU-8K4M2 could not be looked up as a span tag or added to any call chain, and no span, duration or error status for it is known.

Every Prometheus call in this Run failed with status error / reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_label_values 04:52:23Z, execute_prometheus_instant_query 04:52:25Z, 04:52:28Z, 04:52:31Z, 04:52:58Z, 04:53:21Z, 04:54:15Z, 04:54:59Z, 04:55:46Z, metrics_range_query 04:53:01Z, get_metric_names 04:53:53Z, list_prometheus_rules 04:53:53Z, get_all_labels 04:54:45Z, get_series 04:55:22Z, get_prometheus_target 04:52:39Z), so metrics_span_calls_total, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and the state of alert CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh are unknown for the window; a missing series is not zero.

The identifier REQ-EU-8K4M2 was not found anywhere in the sources that answered: an Elasticsearch query_string search over all 1,620 indices inside the window returned no documents (status no_data), and pod-log greps for 'REQ-EU'/'8K4M2' on frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout, payment, product-catalog, cart, currency, email and quote matched no line. These empty results only show those queries matched nothing; they do not prove the request was never logged.

The application log store for namespace app-101 is Loki (promtail job 'payment-api' pushing to http://loki:3100), and no Loki/log-store query tool is enabled in this Run, so any per-request record for REQ-EU-8K4M2 that lives there could not be read.

Which service handled the request, in which region it originated and at what time it was made are all unknown; the complaint gives no timestamp, so no incident instant inside the authorized window could be isolated.

The older documents in the app-185-geo-*-2024.01.0x indices carry 2024 timestamps and sit outside the authorized window, so they were not readable; whether a historical anomaly exists there is unknown.

Secrets could not be read, so the nginx.conf (mounted from a Secret) of prometheus-readonly-proxy could not be inspected, and the reason the Prometheus and Jaeger tools returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE while their pods and Services/Endpoints were present and Ready is not verifiable from the evidence.
next_steps: Re-establish connectivity to the Jaeger query service and the Prometheus read-only proxy, then search spans for the request identifier and inspect checkout PlaceOrder span status and duration for the complaint time.
Query the Loki instance in namespace app-101 (job payment-api) for REQ-EU-8K4M2 and for the customer's request timestamp to obtain the per-request record.
Ask the customer for the timestamp, endpoint and region of the failing request so the correct window and service can be targeted.

Once metrics are reachable, check traces_span_metrics_calls_total by service_name/span_name/status_code and the state of alert CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, and re-check the flagd flag values at the incident time (change history is not integrated in this Run).

content:
server:
  http_listen_port: 9080
positions:
  filename: /tmp/positions.yaml
  sync_period: 10s
  ignore_invalid_yaml: true
clients:
  - url: http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/push
    batchwait: 100ms       # Send batches more frequently
    batchsize: 102400      # 100KB batch size (smaller batches)
    backoff_config:
      min_period: 100ms
      max_period: 1m
      max_retries: 20
    timeout: 10s
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: payment-api
    static_configs:
      - targets:
          - localhost
        labels:
          job: payment-api
          namespace: app-101
          __path__: /var/log/*.log
    pipeline_stages:
      - json:
          expressions:
            timestamp: timestamp
            level: level
            message: message
            service: service
            pod: pod
      - timestamp:
          source: timestamp
          format: RFC3339
      - labels:
          level:
          service:
          pod:

content:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
